module_title: Introduction to Stock Exchanges and SEBI
introduction: A stock exchange is a highly regulated marketplace where previously issued securities (shares, bonds) are bought and sold. In India, the equity market is dominated by two giant exchanges, both of which are closely monitored by a supreme regulatory watchdog: SEBI.

core_concepts.title: BSE (Bombay Stock Exchange)
core_concepts.description: Established in 1875, it is not just India's, but 'Asia's Oldest' stock exchange. It is located on the famous 'Dalal Street' in Mumbai. Historically, trading here was done via an open-outcry system (people shouting prices).

core_concepts.title: NSE (National Stock Exchange)
core_concepts.description: Established in 1992, it is India's largest and most modern stock exchange by daily turnover. It revolutionized the Indian market by introducing a fully automated, screen-based 'electronic trading' system.

core_concepts.title: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
core_concepts.description: SEBI is the apex 'Watchdog' of the Indian capital markets. It was initially set up as a non-statutory body in 1988, but was granted 'Statutory Powers' (legal backing) through the SEBI Act of 1992. Its main objective is to protect the interests of investors and prevent corporate fraud.

important_entities.name: Dalal Street
important_entities.significance: Dalal Street in Mumbai houses the iconic Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers (the BSE building). It is frequently used as a metonym for the entire Indian financial sector (similar to 'Wall Street' in the USA).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic exam trap: 'In which year was SEBI established?' Students jump to 1992. However, it was established in 1988. It only got 'statutory status' in 1992. Read the question carefully!

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: BSE = British Era, NSE = New Era
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: BSE was born during the British colonial period (1875). NSE was born in the modern, electronic era post-LPG reforms (1992).

exam_strategy_tips: Direct Question: 'Which is the oldest stock exchange in Asia?' Answer: BSE.
